name: TCEQ "Sanitary Sewer Overflows (SSO)" dataset on data.texas.gov (8kc5-95uk)
operator: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, Office of Compliance and Enforcement
waters_covered: statewide; receiving_water_body free text (often "NO WATER BODY PROVIDED" / "Not Provided"), river_segment code
access_detail: Socrata SODA: https://data.texas.gov/resource/8kc5-95uk.json ($where, $order, $limit; no key needed for light use). 56,545 rows on 2026-11-03; start dates 2010-09-02 to 2026-08-29; latest received 2026-08-31; rows last updated 2026-09-24 (dataset created 2025-07-17; metadata says "Update Frequency: Semiannually"). 2016-2025 about 3,800 to 6,000 a year; 2026 to August 3,185. About 33,330 rows name a water body. Samples raw/tceq-sso-sample.json, raw/tceq-sso-recent.json, metadata raw/tceq-sso-meta.json.

sample_record.source: Pump line at Lift Station No. 4
sample_record.incident_description: (trimmed) bypass pump line broke; untreated sewage to ground and a storm drain; about 39,000 gallons

cadence: Refreshed in batches (last 2026-09-24, holding reports received to 2026-08-31): one to four months behind. Reports to TCEQ are due within 24 hours (5 working days written).
license: No licence stated in the dataset metadata (licenseId null); data.texas.gov site terms apply.
status_reason: Read through the generic Socrata reader (data/sources/tx-tceq-sso-opendata.yaml): 56,545 rows on 2026-11-07, every one a record; safe fields only (customer_number, incident_action and incident_comment not requested); placed only by the water a row names, never geocoded.
notes: The free text (source, receiving_water_body, incident_description) gets the strict scrub; the operator comes from the row's federal id or data/reference/tx-tceq-permits.json. The research's suggestion to geocode from the description addresses was not taken (owner default 2026-11-07: placement by the named water only).

name: TCEQ "Reporting Unauthorized Discharges and Sanitary Sewer Overflows" guidance page
access_detail: Fetched. 24-hour notice to the regional office; written report in five working days; monthly summary (TCEQ-20756) allowed for small qualifying spills; public/media notice criteria from 30 TAC 319.302; confirmation to TCEQ within 48 hours of public notice.

name: 30 TAC 319.302 Notification Requirements and 319.303 Notice to Local Officials and Local Media
access_detail: Read via LII (the SOS TAC viewer has moved). Notice to local government officials and local media for (1) any spill likely to affect a drinking-water source, (2) 50,000 gallons or more near a drinking-water source or in a sensitive area (recharge zone, karst), (3) 100,000 gallons or more; within 24 hours; hand delivery, fax, email or phone with written follow-up; copy to the TCEQ regional office within 48 hours. 319.303 sets content and precautionary statements ("avoid contact with spill material, soil, or water in the affected area").
status_reason: The public-notice duty: media and local officials only, above 100,000 gallons (or 50,000 near water supplies).

name: Texas General Land Office Texas Beach Watch (BW2025_Summary MapServer)
waters_covered: 174 stations at about 61 Gulf beaches (Aransas, Brazoria, Cameron, Galveston, Harris, Jefferson, Kleberg, Matagorda, Nueces, San Patricio counties)
access_detail: https://gisweb.glo.texas.gov/arcgis/rest/services/BW/BW2025_Summary/MapServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&f=json (public). 174 rows on 2026-11-03; Advisory values "Low" and "Medium" seen (the site maps these to advisory recommended or not; high = advisory); cfu, Measurement ("5 MPN/100ml"), Date of last sample, plus 2023-2025 summary statistics per station (samples, geomean, advisories, percent days under advisory). Behind www.texasbeachwatch.com (ArcGIS JS 3.45; email alert sign-up alertSignup.cfm). Sample raw/tbw-sample.json.
cadence: Weekly March to October, every two weeks otherwise; advisory resampled every 24 hours. Layer updated as results are entered.
history: current state plus 2023-2025 summaries; the service name changes yearly (BW2025_Summary)
status_reason: Read through the generic ArcGIS reader (data/sources/tx-glo-beach-watch.yaml): 174 stations on 2026-11-07 (Low 162, Medium 12, High 0); High is the program's advisory, Medium its label.
notes: Watch for the service name changing (BW2026_...). 2026-11-21: www.texasbeachwatch.com answered 302 to GLO's home page and the layer timed out (this Mac and GitHub's runner) during GLO's announced weekend maintenance of texasbeachwatch.com and some map applications from 2026-11-20 17:00 Central; the citation stays.

name: City of Houston Public Works monthly SSO reports (consent decree Paragraph 61)
operator: City of Houston, Houston Public Works
waters_covered: Houston bayous (Buffalo, Brays, Sims, White Oak, Greens, Halls)
access_detail: HTML page https://www.houstonpublicworks.org/wastewater-cd linking one PDF per month ("Monthly SSO Report - <Month YYYY>", April 2021 to September 2026 on 2026-11-17; irregular file names, the month read from the link title), filed under the 2021 wastewater consent decree (U.S. and Texas v. City of Houston, 4:18-cv-03368, S.D. Tex.; the cover letter cites Paragraph 61). Table: SSO ID, TPDES permit, address, flow location, reached waters of the US (Yes/No), estimated gallons, structure type, cause, start and end date and time, average flow (GPM), corrective action; the month's total, notifications to the public and the City's notes under it; a map page of points.
sample_record: SSO 68784, September 2026: WQ0010495003, Graustark St (house number removed), Storm Sewer (not contained), reached waters of the US: Yes, 567 gallons, Manhole, Grease Blockage, 9/10/2026 9:33 AM to 12:15 PM, 4 GPM, Cleaned and Disinfected; Cleared Main Line
fills_event_fields: cause, structure type, flow location, corrective action
cannot_fill: the receiving water (taken from TCEQ's record of the same overflow where it names one)
coordinates (the map is a PDF; no geocoding of the street)
cadence: monthly, two to seven weeks after the month ends (September 2026 posted October 16, 2026)
history: April 2021 to date on the page; read from January 2024
status_reason: Read hourly by pipeline/ingest/tx_houston_sso_monthly.py from 2026-11-17 (--backfill for the months from January 2024): one record per row, start and end to the minute, the City's reached-water flag kept. 33 reports read on 2026-11-17, 4,407 rows (1,409 marked as reaching waters of the US), each month's count equal to its stated total. TCEQ's record of the same overflow (3,017 rows met one on TCEQ's Harris County rows from 2023) is linked as the same event, the City's row shown.

name: Texas DSHS Status of Shellfish Harvesting Areas (status table)
operator: Texas Department of State Health Services, Seafood and Aquatic Life Group
waters_covered: Texas Gulf coast shellfish harvest areas TX 1 to TX 34 (by DSHS's code)
access_detail: HTML table Harvest Area / Public Harvest Area Status / Private Oyster Area Status / Reason for Status under a dated heading; a dated PDF copy
sample_record: TX 14 | Closed | Closed | TPWD Action, Rainfall (table dated 11.16.2026)
cannot_fill: closure start (the table gives none: the first read is used)
the area's outline (DSHS's layer does not carry the table's codes)
history: none on the page (a dated PDF of each table)
status_reason: Read by the tx-dshs-shellfish-harvest-status ingester (ingest.tx_dshs_shellfish): one shellfish_closure record per area listed Closed with rainfall, runoff, flooding, a spill, wastewater or sewage among DSHS's reasons, from the first read that lists it; closures for TPWD action alone (seasons, resource management) are left out, and an unknown reason is unread. Every closure is listed with DSHS's code and placed on no water. Table dated 11.16.2026: 28 areas, 4 closed with rainfall among the reasons (TX 14, TX 19, TX 20, TX 21), 16 closed for TPWD action only, 8 open.
notes: DSHS's harvest-area layer (Texas Shellfish Harvest Area Viewer, 2026-27) names its 287 polygons by bay and class; tying the table's TX codes to them needs DSHS's legal descriptions (PDF).
